templates.name: Proxmox VE (Example Music)
templates.description:
Companion template for ansible/playbooks/proxmox/site.yml (+ bootstrap-new-node.yml). Copied from zabbix_template_cloudpanel.json's own generator and expanded, 2026-10-20, following a shopping-list-first review of all 10 numbered playbooks, bootstrap-new-node.yml, first-boot.sh, and group_vars/pvenodes/main.yml.

SECTIONS
  Packages: pve_packages (group_vars/pvenodes/main.yml), deduped against common_packages -- jq/net-tools/tree/molly-guard/nmap/parted/vim/zsh/grc/unattended-upgrades are already checked by linuxtools. open-vm-tools is macro-gated ({$PROXMOX.OPEN_VM_TOOLS_EXPECTED}) -- only installed on a VMware guest, real bare-metal nodes never get it.
  Custom scripts: every script 40-scripts.yml deploys (from bootstrap/web/proxmox/ and this family's own files/), each with TWO items -- vfs.file.exists AND vfs.file.cksum, the latter compared against a per-script {$PROXMOX.CKSUM.*} macro holding the real committed source's own cksum (computed directly, not fabricated). Rudimentary drift/version detection -- a hand-patched file on one node (testing a fix before committing it) shows up immediately against every other node's still-matching checksum, same intent 40-scripts.yml's own header already documents.
  Config/data files: /etc/example-music's 3 CSVs + nodeinfo.json (same pattern as linuxtools, via 30-example-music.yml instead), plus the unattended-upgrades-pve apt-pin, proxmorph's own apt hook, and the NIC-guard credentials example.
  nodeinfo.json contents: identical base-schema pattern to every other template, PLUS this family's own real nodeinfo_extra fields (node_ip/gateway, 30-example-music.yml) via the same JSONPATH-dependents technique proven on firewall/ansible-node -- unlike cloudpanel, this family genuinely has role-specific extras.
  Systemd timers: the 4 real PVE maintenance timers, system.run[systemctl is-enabled ...] (classic agent, NOT the agent2-only systemd.unit.info key). proxmox-replica-nic-guard's own RUNTIME OUTPUT already has a separate, pre-existing template (zabbix_template_proxmox_nicguard.yaml) -- deliberately not duplicated here, this template only checks the script file + timer.
  Network: vmbr1 (marker-based, matches 36-vmbr1.yml's own Ansible-managed-block comment) and vmbr0's static-vs-DHCP state (visibility only -- a node mid-onboarding may legitimately still be on DHCP). /etc/network/interfaces is a plain 0644 file (confirmed in the code) -- no NetworkManager-style permission workaround needed, unlike cloudpanel's own network check.
  Pools: cluster-wide (pvesh), 1h delay. Count comparison (sites.csv rows vs. pvesh's own pool count) rather than a full set-difference -- bash process substitution isn't available under system.run's POSIX sh, and a count comparison catches the real, practical failure mode (new site, pool not yet created) without a fragile pipeline. Known limitation, documented on the trigger itself: doesn't name WHICH site, and tolerates MORE pools than sites (35-pools.yml only ever adds).
  ZFS redundancy: the same vdev-counting regex as 00-preflight.yml's one-time onboarding gate, promoted to an ongoing 24h check -- a disk failing out of a mirror after onboarding is exactly what routine monitoring should catch.
  V2V/virt tooling: the two mingw-srvany exes (known caveat -- not every upstream RPM build ships both, documented on the item itself, not hidden), VirtIO driver extraction. proxmoxbmc (install + service) and all 6 BIOS ROM files are written but DISABLED -- both genuinely off by default with no real source URL configured anywhere yet; enabling now would be permanent false positives on every real node. Ready to enable once a real pve_proxmoxbmc_deb_url/pve_bios_rom_base_url exists.
  Identity/access: ansible user in the kvm group (simple length()=0 trigger on a /etc/group regexp, 1h). Also added /etc/sudoers.d/ansible and /home/ansible/.ssh/authorized_keys existence checks -- confirmed by re-reading linuxtools' own real item list that neither is actually checked there (an earlier assumption that they were already redundant turned out wrong on verification).
  proxmorph: hardware sensor support, mirroring 46-proxmorph.yml's own detect_sensors() precondition (4 chip families) -- visibility only, no trigger, since lacking a supported sensor chip is a real hardware limitation, not a fault. Whether proxmorph itself installed correctly is covered by the apt-hook exists check above, not a separate 'package installed' item (proxmorph isn't a real .deb package).

NOT YET LIVE-IMPORTED OR LIVE-TESTED against a real Zabbix server or a real zabbix-agent -- same status as every other template in this series.

IMPORT: configuration.import, rules: createMissing+updateExisting+deleteMissing on items/triggers, createMissing+updateExisting on template_groups/templates.

Count comparison only -- doesn't identify WHICH site, and deliberately tolerates MORE pools than sites (35-pools.yml only ever adds pools, never removes, so a legacy/renamed site's old pool surviving isn't itself a fault).

items.name: ZFS rpool: ONLINE vdev (disk) count
items.key: system.run["zpool status rpool 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^\s+\S+\s+ONLINE\s+[0-9]+\s+[0-9]+\s+[0-9]+\s*$' | grep -vE '^\s+(rpool|mirror|raidz[123]?|spare|replacing|indirect|log|cache|special|dedup)(-[0-9]+)?\s' | wc -l",wait]
items.description: Same leaf-disk-counting regex as 00-preflight.yml's own one-time single-disk onboarding check (excludes pool-name/vdev-group lines rather than matching specific device-name patterns, so it's correct regardless of by-id vs. short kernel device naming) -- promoted here to an ongoing check, since a disk failing out of a mirror after onboarding is exactly the kind of thing routine monitoring should catch, not just a point-in-time gate.

triggers.expression: last(/Proxmox VE (Example Music)/system.run["zpool status rpool 2>/dev/null | grep -E '^\s+\S+\s+ONLINE\s+[0-9]+\s+[0-9]+\s+[0-9]+\s*$' | grep -vE '^\s+(rpool|mirror|raidz[123]?|spare|replacing|indirect|log|cache|special|dedup)(-[0-9]+)?\s' | wc -l",wait])<2
triggers.name: Hey! {HOST.NAME} - ZFS rpool has no redundancy (< 2 disks)
triggers.description: rpool has fewer than 2 ONLINE vdevs -- no redundancy, will lose all data if the remaining disk fails. See docs/proxmox/zfs-raid0-to-raid1.md.

items.name: proxmorph: hardware sensor support
items.key: system.run["sensors -j 2>/dev/null | grep -qE 'coretemp-isa-|k10temp-pci-|nvme-pci-|drivetemp-scsi-|fan[0-9]*_input' && echo supported || echo unsupported",wait]
items.description: Mirrors 46-proxmorph.yml's own detect_sensors() precondition check (same 4 chip-pattern families). 'unsupported' is a real hardware limitation on this specific box, not a fault -- visibility only, no trigger. The apt-hook exists check above (/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/99proxmorph) already covers whether proxmorph itself installed correctly.
